title: Layered Illustrated Workshop — representative interaction slice
hypothesis: A compact painterly sprite vocabulary can make the fixed-camera puzzle feel like an intimate glass workshop while engine-authored geometry remains the sole authority for interaction, orientation, beam topology, and state.

camera.cameraType: fixed Node2D canvas; no Camera2D transform

method.name: layered-sprite-hybrid
method.decorativeLayers: ImageGen-authored raster backdrop and four-quadrant instrument atlas
method.semanticLayers: Godot CanvasItem geometry derived from simulated state and one shared nonblocking presentation clock
method.movingContingency: The solver-aligned reflector spine, focus contour, beam-contact sensor aperture, shutter halves, post-travel receiver settle, and beam remain crisp native geometry over the painterly layers.

resources.purpose: Authoritative gameplay state plus layered presentation seam
Shipping-camera capture into mutable design evidence
Deterministic mirror-semantics and live-presentation boundary checks
Decorative brass mount, glass reflector, source collar, and receiver housing
Exact ImageGen prompts, source mode, and byte-preserving postprocess record

quadrants.topLeft: aged-brass empty mount reused by mirrors and sensor
quadrants.topRight: vertical smoke-blue reflector blade rotated around its exact cell center
quadrants.bottomLeft: amber source collar without a baked beam
quadrants.bottomRight: cold receiver housing without a baked arrived state

atlas.pivotRule: Every transformable layer is drawn from a centered destination rectangle and rotated around cell_center(cell).
atlas.maskRule: Atlas alpha is decorative only and never changes the full-cell input hit region.
atlas.stateRule: No focus, orientation spine, contact fill, shutter state, receiver fill, or beam path is stored in the atlas.

implementedSurfaces.scope: Finished material island for source, three reusable mirrors, sensor, linkage, shutter, receiver, board, beam, lesson, and reset control.
The same background, source, receiver, mirror assembly, beam, and control surface render without topology-specific repainting.

Always-amber native beam with dark separation stroke, narrow hot core, contact facets, leading mote, and a 0.42-second reveal restarted by ordinary recompute timing. Receiver geometry supplies the cool arrival response after full travel.
Authoritative orientation changes immediately through apply_action; a 0.18-second native visual quarter-turn settles around the same cell pivot.
Authoritative latch state updates immediately; the sensor changes from hollow to filled and the shutter from one blocker to two retracted halves only when the shared reveal reaches sensor contact.
One restrained right-side turn legend, arrow/Tab focus hint, and reset control; observations dashboard and rotation counter are absent.

motionSequence.intent: Initial finale route; cold sensor and continuous closed shutter.
Receiver-side mirror prepared; no false arrival.
Lower route mirror prepared; topology remains incomplete.
Upper mirror contacts the sensor through live reveal timing; filled aperture and split shutter are visible.
Full open-but-incomplete state persists after contact without a color-only label.
Upper mirror returns; leading beam travels through the opened lower route.
Beam arrives through the same live reveal path; receiver changes from hollow to filled and completes its value-bright settle.

reuseConstraints: Reuse atlas layers only at centered cell pivots; never derive input masks from alpha.
Keep beam, orientation, focus, sensor contact, shutter geometry, and receiver arrival engine-controlled and above decorative art.
The background may be reused because it contains no cell grid, route, piece, beam, or state.
Do not invent a topology-specific repaint or a bespoke mirror asset for another puzzle.
At other cameras or cell scales, revalidate sprite edge clarity, beam separation, and pivot stability before expansion.
deliberateOmissions: No bespoke finish for WAKE THE WORKSHOP or USE WHAT CHANGED.
No production title or won-screen art beyond compatibility with shared colors and type scale.
No asset family variants, shelves, tools, hands, decorative labels, particles, fog, bloom, audio, camera change, or 3D conversion.
No topology, orientation, beam, contact, or state feedback baked into static assets.
No claim that deterministic completion or model inspection establishes fun.

validation.evidenceBoundary: Deterministic validation establishes stability and contract preservation only.
